text:
tomas: Heads up — noticed a regression on paged-attn after yesterday's runtime change. small-batch (B<=4) requests hitting FlashAttention2 path show 2-3x tail latency on 768/2048 seq workloads.

maria: repro steps?

tomas: repro harness: mix of chat streams, seq=768, kv cache enabled, kv-slot compaction on. baseline before change: p95 ~ 65ms. after: p95 ~ 180ms with big variance. nvprof/cuprof shows spikes at kernel select and then a lot of async memcpy stalls.

raj: do we see increased page faults?

tomas: yes — host-side telemetry: "GPU_PAGE_FAULTS_RATE" jumps from ~20/s to ~1200/s while the requests run. also saw OOM-like transient backpressure on the paged-kv allocator (failed allocations then immediate frees).

aline: hmm. did the kernel chooser logic change for short batches? could be we're switching to a fused-F1 path that expects contiguous KV layout.

oliver: @tomas can you paste the kernel selection trace?

tomas: pasted below (from debug=kernel-chooser):

```
[2026-03-15T12:02:03] req=0x7fa2: choose_kernel -> heur: flash2_if_small_batch
[2026-03-15T12:02:03] model=fl8b-3B seq=768 batch=1 kv_pages=42 frag_score=0.67
[2026-03-15T12:02:03] kernels:
  - flash2 (expected_latency=48ms)
  - paged_fused (expected_latency=55ms)
chosen: flash2
[2026-03-15T12:02:03] post-select: alloc_hint=contiguous_high
[2026-03-15T12:02:04] alloc failed -> fallback slab-split
```

maria: frag_score=0.67 is high — that means our slotmap has fragmentation across hot and cold pages. flash2's memcpy-heavy path probably thrashes the GPU->host page working set.

raj: Could the batching sampler be biasing toward smaller batches in the new traffic mix? if we push batching window slightly up it might pick paged_fused which tolerates fragmented KV.

aline: Another angle — the allocator returned a "contiguous_high" hint but our pager currently honors hints best-effort; when it falls back to slab-split it scatters KV across pages, increasing cross-page accesses. For FlashAttention2 that's bad because it expects long contiguous KV streams to avoid repeated page faults during KV cache walks.

oliver: Any quick mitigations we can try on staging?

maria: - Force kernel chooser to prefer paged_fused for batch<=4 on the cohort to verify hypothesis.
  - Disable compaction-on-write or reduce compaction aggressiveness (kv.compact_threshold -> 0.2).
  - Temporarily change allocator to prefer "packed" placement for new slots.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline: triggered rollout "probe/flash2-bias-fix" to canary pool (10 hosts) by maria at 12:14 UTC

tomas: Ran the canary with kernel bias to paged_fused and p95 dropped to 72ms — close to baseline. page_faults_rate back to ~35/s. Looks like chooser + allocator interplay is root cause.

raj: Nice. We still want flash2 performance for clean VM state. Could we augment chooser to add a frag_score threshold: if frag_score > 0.4 avoid flash2 even if batch is small?

aline: Yeah propose: chooser decision = flash2_if_small_batch AND frag_score <= frag_threshold AND contiguous_hint==true. Default frag_threshold=0.4. Also add telemetry for "chooser_mismatch" when chosen kernel suffers >2x expected latency.

oliver: For allocator: add a fast-path compaction when fragmentation is local to the model's slot range. Cheap compaction could reduce frag_score quickly. Also consider prefetching hot KV pages before kernel runs.

maria: Prefetch is promising but increases memory bandwidth. let's add an adaptive prefetch: only when page_faults_rate>threshold and frag_score>threshold.

tomas: I'll spin a PR: chooser change + frag telemetry + a knob to force paged_fused for small batches. Also will add a quick allocator patch to prefer packing new slots adjacent to existing model pages.

oliver: Can we add a small synthetic test to our perf harness that intentionally fragments KV then runs flash2 to catch regressions early?

maria: yes, add a test that does: allocate N small KV slots interleaved with frees to create scattering, then run 200 requests through flash2 path and assert p95 < X. put it in nightly perf.

sre-bot: alert suppressed: gpu-pagefaults spike alert (rule: gpu.pagefaults.rate > 500/s) — currently firing on canary hosts, muted for 30m while investigation continues.

tomas: thanks everyone. action items:
- tomas: PR for chooser + telemetry + allocator packing (WIP).
- maria: keep canary running and collect traces for next 6h.
- raj: add batching-sampler ab test to slightly increase batch window in case traffic changes.
- aline: design quick compaction micro-op for allocator (low cost).

maria: updated canary: 10/10 hosts healthy, latency back to expected. will promote to 30 hosts after additional smoke. :thumbsup:

oliver: nice detective work :mag:
